result.title: ProMemAgent: Long-Horizon Proactive Assistance with Context-Aware Prospective Memory from Sensory Perceptions
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are moving beyond reactive responses toward proactive assistance that anticipates user needs without explicit requests. However, existing proactive agents primarily address immediate needs, while many everyday situations involve delayed intentions that can only be acted on hours or days later. Humans handle such intentions through prospective memory, the ability to remember to act on an intention when the right moment arises. In this paper, we introduce ProMemAgent, the first proactive agent to incorporate prospective memory over everyday sensory contexts for long-horizon proactive assistance. ProMemAgent organizes past sensory perceptions (e.g., egocentric video and audio) into context-aware memory, generating prospective cues and linking earlier events with subsequent developments for future retrieval. Given the current context, it retrieves relevant past events and performs memory-augmented proactive reasoning to determine whether assistance is needed. We further introduce CPMBench, the first benchmark for evaluating long-horizon proactive assistance over sensory contexts, comprising 1,000 instances across eight everyday categories. Extensive experiments show that ProMemAgent achieves the best memory retrieval performance and consistently outperforms all baselines on long-horizon proactive assistance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ProMemAgent，把日常第一视角视频与音频组织为上下文感知的前瞻性记忆，生成记忆线索并检索相关过往事件，再做记忆增强的主动推理以判断当下是否需要提供协助，并构建 CPMBench 基准进行评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「由记忆检索证据决定是否介入」的流程可供核查与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 中的证据筛选和停止决策相关线索，但未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成与使用，属方法层面的间接參考。
